title: How Codeium Breaks Through the Ceiling for Retrieval: Kevin Hou
talk_summary: Kevin Hou argues vector embeddings hit a ceiling for code retrieval and describes Codeium's M-query: parallel LLM calls to score many candidate files, then rank with workflow signals. He also shows how they build product-led evals from PR commit messages mapped to modified files and measure recall@50.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build an eval from PR commits: the commit message is the query and the modified files are the ground truth, then measure how much ground truth appears in the top 50 retrieved items.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we looked at PRS like this it's broken down into commits those commits we can extract and actually match them with the modified files
takeaways.numbers: recall@50; top 50 items; public models showed reduced performance on commit-message retrieval

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of relying only on vector similarity, they run parallel LLM calls to reason over each candidate item and produce a high-confidence relevance ranking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're now making parallel calls to an llm to actually reason over each one of those items
takeaways.numbers: thousands of LLMs in parallel; results in seconds or milliseconds

takeaways.technique: Cheap parallel ranking instead of long-context stuffing
takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid putting huge repos into long-context models because of latency and cost, and instead spend compute on many small parallel relevance calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we throw more compute at it right but of course that can't come with uh absurd absurd uh uh cost
takeaways.numbers: 325k tokens cited for long-context ingestion; a small repo can exceed 1M tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue needle-in-a-haystack retrieval benchmarks miss code search, which needs multiple relevant files, so they evaluate multi-document recall instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code search requires multiple different needles

takeaways.what_they_do: They roll changes out to a small percentage of users, measure thumbs up/down and acceptance, then iterate back into the eval loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were able to roll this out to a small percentage of our users

takeaways.what_they_do: They combine LLM relevance with active files, neighboring directories, recent commits, and the current ticket to choose top documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: things like your active files your neighboring director your most recent commits
